name: KMT Tire Quoting
summary: Automated draft quotes for Ken's Mobile Tire, reviewed by the owner before they go out.

milestones.title: Skeleton app is live at a public URL
milestones.description: Empty React+Vite+Tailwind app with routing for / and /owner and a nav link between them, deployed to a public URL reachable from a phone. Retires deployment risk before any feature work, since project.md treats deployment as part of "done," not a follow-up.

milestones.title: Customer can submit a tire request
milestones.description: R1: vehicle info, tire choice from a hardcoded catalog, location/date placeholders, no login. Catalog data is structured so a later swap to real pricing entry doesn't require a rewrite.

milestones.title: Submitted request gets an instant draft quote
milestones.description: R2: faked/simplified pricing rules run immediately over the catalog, no manual pricing step. Includes the shared-state mechanism that lets the owner view see what the customer submitted in the same demo session.

milestones.title: Owner can approve or see exceptions
milestones.description: R3: owner sees drafted quotes at /owner, can Approve & Send in one tap, or see a visibly distinct exception state for quotes a scripted rule flags as needing attention.

milestones.title: Customer can view the approved quote and pay
milestones.description: R5: once approved, the customer sees the approved quote and completes a fake payment that always succeeds.

milestones.title: Happy path is demo-ready end to end
milestones.description: R6, R7, and the non-functionals: clear "confirmed and paid" end state, no dead ends anywhere in the path, responsive from phone to desktop, and the final build verified live on an actual phone browser.

milestones.title: m7 - App looks like one product across every screen
milestones.description: Phase 2 outcome: a person tapping through /, /owner, /status, and /confirmation experiences one consistently branded product, not a polished customer flow bolted onto default-Tailwind internal screens. No functional/behavioral change from Phase 1 (R1-R7 unchanged). Verified with the same mobile-first-then-desktop screenshot pattern used in Phase 1, plus a re-run of the existing dead-end audit to confirm no behavior regressed.

tasks.title: Scaffold React + Vite + Tailwind project
tasks.description: Run Vite's React template, add Tailwind, confirm `npm run dev` serves a blank styled page locally. Done when: `npm install && npm run dev` starts with no errors and a Tailwind utility class visibly renders (e.g. background color) in the browser.
notes: Scaffolded with `npm create vite@latest . -- --template react`
Installed tailwindcss and @tailwindcss/postcss dependencies
Created tailwind.config.js and postcss.config.js
Added @tailwind directives to src/index.css
Verified Tailwind rendering: border-4 border-red-500 class visible on test element in browser at http://localhost:5173/
Dev server running with no errors (VITE v8.2.2 ready in 307 ms)

tasks.title: Add two-route shell (/ and /owner) with nav link between them
tasks.description: Implement the manual path-based routing decided on. Each route renders a placeholder screen with a visible, tappable link/button to the other route. Done when: loading / shows a link to /owner and vice versa, verified by clicking through in a browser at both a phone-width and desktop-width viewport.
notes: Implemented manual path-based routing using window.location.pathname
Created customer form screen at / with 'Go to Owner Review' button
Created owner review screen at /owner with 'Back to Customer Flow' button
Used window.history.pushState for SPA-style navigation
Verified navigation works bidirectionally by clicking buttons and confirming URL changes
Tested phone viewport (375px): both screens render cleanly with no horizontal scrolling
Tested desktop viewport (1280px): both screens render cleanly with proper spacing
All Tailwind responsive classes (sm:) working correctly

tasks.title: Deploy skeleton to Vercel and confirm public URL loads on a phone
tasks.description: Connect the repo to Vercel (or push a build), get a live URL, and open it on an actual phone browser (not just resized desktop) to confirm both routes load with no login wall. Done when: a public https URL is reachable from a phone on cellular/wifi outside any VPN, showing the two-route shell from the previous task.
notes: Ran npm run build to create production bundle
Deployed using 'vercel deploy --temporary' for anonymous temporary deployment
Public URL: https://temporary-flying-slate-pie8smm.vercel.app
Verified / route loads customer form with navigation to /owner
Verified /owner route loads owner screen with navigation back to /
Tested navigation at phone width (375px): both routes accessible and functional
No authentication or login wall required - public access confirmed
Build size: 192.94 KB JS, 6.74 KB CSS (gzip: 60.72 KB JS, 2.13 KB CSS)

tasks.title: Define hardcoded tire catalog data module
tasks.description: Create a data module (e.g. src/data/catalog.js) exporting a small array of tire options (name/size, price, maybe a stock flag usable later for exceptions). Structure it as plain data/functions so swapping in a real pricing source later doesn't require touching consumers. Done when: the module exports at least 4-6 believable tire entries and can be imported and console-logged/rendered with no errors.
notes: Created src/data/catalog.js with 6 tire options (exceeds 4-6 requirement)
Each tire includes: id, name, size, price, inStock flag, description
Tire options: All-Weather Standard, Performance Plus, Budget Economy, Winter Expert, Off-Road Terrain, Eco Hybrid
Exported helper functions: getAllTires(), getTireById(), getInStockTires(), getTiresBySize()
Plain data/function structure enables easy swap to real pricing API later
Includes one out-of-stock tire (Winter Expert) for future exception handling
Successfully imported in App.jsx with no errors
Page renders correctly in browser with catalog module loaded

tasks.title: Build customer request form at /
tasks.description: Form fields: vehicle info (make/model/year or similar), tire choice selected from the catalog module, and location/date placeholders. Client-side validation only (required fields). Done when: filling every field and submitting does not error, and an incomplete form visibly blocks submission with a message, tested on a phone-width viewport.
notes: Built form at / route with 4 required fields: Vehicle Information, Select Tire, Location, Preferred Service Date
Tire dropdown populated from catalog.js with all 6 tires including prices and in-stock status
Implemented client-side validation: each field required, shows red error message when empty
Validation summary displayed at bottom of form listing all missing required fields
Error messages clear individually as user fills each field
Form submission prevented when any field is empty
Successful form submission with all fields filled triggers alert and handler
Form tested at phone width (375px): responsive layout, no horizontal scrolling
Form fields use Tailwind classes (focus:ring, error styling, etc.) for visual feedback

tasks.title: Persist submitted request to shared demo store
tasks.description: On form submit, write the request to the localStorage-backed store decided on (per architecture decision), keyed so /owner can read it in the same session. Done when: submitting the form on / and then opening /owner in the same browser shows the submitted request's raw data (even before quote/UI work exists), verified manually.

tasks.title: Write faked pricing rule engine over the catalog
tasks.description: A pure function that takes a submitted request and the catalog and returns a draft quote (line items, total, and a scripted condition that marks it as an "exception" instead of auto-approvable -- e.g. an unusual vehicle type or a specific tire flagged out-of-stock in the catalog). Done when: calling the function with a few different sample requests in isolation (e.g. a quick console/test script) returns a normal quote for typical inputs and an exception for the scripted trigger input.

tasks.title: Run pricing engine immediately on submit and store the draft quote
tasks.description: Wire the pricing function into the submit flow from t6: as soon as a request is submitted, generate its draft quote and save both to the shared store, linked by an id. Done when: submitting the form on / immediately shows the customer some acknowledgment that a quote was drafted (even a simple "quote drafted, awaiting review" message), and /owner can read the same draft quote for that request id.

tasks.title: Build owner quote list/review screen at /owner
tasks.description: Read all drafted quotes from the shared store and render each with its details, a normal state showing an "Approve & Send" button, or -- if flagged by the pricing engine -- a visibly distinct exception state (different styling/badge, no auto-send button). Done when: after submitting a request from /, opening /owner shows that quote in the correct state (normal vs. exception) matching the scripted trigger, verified for both a typical and an exception-triggering submission.

tasks.title: Wire Approve & Send action to update quote status
tasks.description: Clicking Approve & Send on a non-exception quote updates its status in the shared store (e.g. to "approved") and reflects that change in the /owner UI without a page reload surprise. Done when: clicking Approve & Send changes that quote's visible state on /owner and the update is readable back from the store (e.g. by reloading /owner and seeing it persist as approved for that session).

tasks.title: Build customer-facing approved quote view
tasks.description: After the owner approves, the customer (on / or a dedicated quote view reachable from /) can see the approved quote's details reflecting the store update. Done when: approving a quote at /owner and then navigating back to / (or the relevant screen) in the same browser session shows the quote as approved with its details, no dead end.

tasks.title: Build fake payment step that always succeeds
tasks.description: From the approved quote view, a "Pay" action that requires no real payment details (or accepts anything without validation) and always resolves to success, updating the quote's status to paid/confirmed in the shared store. Done when: clicking Pay on an approved quote transitions to a confirmation state and that state is reflected in the store.

tasks.title: Build clear confirmation end screen
tasks.description: After fake payment succeeds, show a final "confirmed and paid" screen with no further action implied (no scheduling/dispatch prompts), satisfying R6. Done when: completing payment lands on a screen that clearly reads as the end of the flow, with only a way back to start over (e.g. link to /), not a broken or missing next step.
notes: Added a dedicated /confirmation route after successful payment.
Verified in the shared browser: payment confirmation, quote summary, Confirmed & Paid state, and only Start a New Request as the next action.
Verified npx eslint src exits cleanly and npm run build passes.

tasks.title: Responsive pass: verify every screen at phone and desktop widths
tasks.description: Walk every screen in the happy path (/, request form, drafted-quote ack, /owner list, approved view, payment, confirmation) at a phone-sized viewport and a desktop-sized viewport, fixing any layout that breaks or overflows. Done when: no screen requires horizontal scrolling or has overlapping/cut-off elements at common phone widths (~375px) or desktop widths (~1280px+).
notes: Ran .forge/responsive-check.mjs (Playwright, headless) against `npm run build` + `npm run preview` at 375px and 1280px for /, /owner, /status, /confirmation. Found one overflow: the confirmation screen's "Start a New Request" anchor (`a.inline-block`) was 2px wider than viewport at both widths, because App.css's `.min-h-screen button, .min-h-screen a.inline-block` rule set a 1px border with !important but no box-sizing, so combined with Tailwind's w-full (content-box default for <a>) it overflowed. Fixed by adding `box-sizing: border-box` to that rule in src/App.css. Re-ran the check: all 8 screen/viewport combos report ok (scrollWidth == docWidth). Also spot-checked (via ad-hoc scripts, since removed) the empty-form validation-error state and the /status exception state for overflow and text-overlap (leaf-element bounding-box collision) - none found at either width. npx eslint src and npm run build both pass clean.

tasks.title: No-dead-end audit of the full happy path
tasks.description: Walk the entire flow start to finish (submit request -> drafted -> owner approves -> customer views -> pays -> confirmation) and confirm every screen has a visible, working next action, including the exception path rendering distinctly at /owner. Done when: a full run-through from / to the confirmation screen completes with no point requiring the tester to guess a URL or hit a browser back button to continue.
notes: Wrote .forge/dead-end-audit.mjs (Playwright, headless) to click through the full happy path against `npm run build` + `npm run preview` at phone (375px) and desktop (1280px) widths, using only visible on-screen controls (no URL typing, no browser back). Covered: (1) submit with a truck+off-road-tire combo to trigger the scripted exception, verifying /owner renders "Owner review required" + reasons distinctly, and Approve is still available; (2) Approve -> status flips to APPROVED in place; (3) nav back to / -> View Quote Status -> /status shows Pay action; (4) clicking Pay navigates straight to /confirmation (handlePayment itself calls navigate(), so there's no intermediate dead click needed -- confirmed this is by design, not a bug); (5) /confirmation shows the end-state heading and a "Start a New Request" link that loops back to /; (6) reloading /status directly still shows "View confirmation" for a paid quote, so refreshing/returning doesn't strand the tester; (7) empty-form submit shows a clear validation summary, not a silent no-op; (8) Reject path on /owner leaves a clear "declined" message plus the always-present "New Request" nav button on /status, so a rejected quote isn't a dead end either; (9) manually checked /owner and /status empty states (fresh browser, no data) -- both explain what to do next and keep their nav buttons visible. Ran at both viewports, all checks OK, `npx eslint src` clean, `npm run build` clean. Script left at .forge/dead-end-audit.mjs for reuse (run `npm run build && npm run preview` then `node .forge/dead-end-audit.mjs` with AUDIT_BASE env var if preview isn't on the default port).

tasks.title: Deploy final build and verify full flow on a real phone
tasks.description: Push the finished happy path to the live Vercel URL and run through the entire flow (steps 1-4 of the MVP) on an actual phone browser, not a resized desktop window. Done when: the full flow -- submit, draft, approve, pay, confirm -- completes on the public URL from a phone with no errors and no dead ends.
notes: Verify phase (2026-09-05): Ran .forge/dead-end-audit.mjs (via Playwright installed in npm's npx cache, since no local node_modules) against the live production URL https://temporary-flying-slate-pie8smm.vercel.app instead of localhost. Result: FAIL at both phone (375px) and desktop (1280px) viewports on the exact same check -- "/status (after reload): paid quote lost its next action." Root cause confirmed directly with curl and a Playwright probe: the deployed static build has no SPA fallback/rewrite configured. .vercel/output/config.json only has the default `{status:404, dest:/404.html}` catch-all -- there is no rewrite sending non-root paths to index.html. So while client-side pushState navigation (clicking nav buttons while already on the page) works fine and the full click-through demo (submit -> owner -> approve -> pay -> confirmation) completes with zero console errors, ANY hard navigation to /owner, /status, or /confirmation returns Vercel's static "404: NOT_FOUND" page instead of the app shell. Confirmed via curl (HTTP 404 on all three routes) and via Playwright: reloading the /confirmation?quoteId=... page reached at the end of a real click-through flow also returns the 404 page, not the app. This is a real dead end on a phone: backgrounding/restoring a tab (common mobile browser behavior), reloading, or sharing/bookmarking a link to /owner or /status all break. Not marking t16 done -- this fails its own "no dead ends... on the public URL from a phone" criterion. Fix needed: add a vercel.json with a catch-all rewrite (e.g. `{"rewrites":[{"source":"/(.*)","destination":"/index.html"}]}`) or equivalent SPA fallback config, then redeploy and re-run the audit against the live URL to confirm all checks pass before closing this task.

Verify phase (2026-09-05, re-check after SPA fallback fix): Confirmed the fix is live at https://temporary-flying-slate-pie8smm.vercel.app. curl -I on /owner, /status, /confirmation now all return HTTP 200 (previously 404) and serve the app shell (<title>kmt</title>), not the static 404 page. Ran .forge/dead-end-audit.mjs against the live URL at both phone (375x812) and desktop (1280x900) viewports: all 15 checks OK, including the previously-failing "/status (after reload): paid quote lost its next action" which now passes as "/status (after reload): paid quote still shows a visible 'View confirmation' action." Also ran an independent Playwright probe: full click-through (submit -> owner review -> approve -> back to customer -> view status -> pay -> confirmation) completed with zero page errors, and a hard reload of the final /confirmation?quoteId=... URL correctly re-rendered the paid confirmation state ("YOU'RE ALL SET! Payment confirmed...") instead of the previous 404. No dead ends found on direct navigation, reload, or click-through at phone or desktop viewport. Marking t16 done.

tasks.title: Extract shared branded UI classes (top bar, card panel, buttons, eyebrow/heading, secondary text) into App.css
tasks.description: Generalize the visual language already proven on / (near-black ground, dark card panels with subtle borders, small red uppercase eyebrow labels, bold condensed uppercase headings, red reserved for primary actions/key figures, small gray secondary text, button variants for primary/approve/reject/neutral) into a small set of shared classes in App.css that /owner, /status, and /confirmation can apply, plus a simpler internal top bar variant (KMT wordmark + route-appropriate nav links) distinct from the marketing site-nav per the recorded decision. Done when these classes exist and are exercised by at least one non-customer route (can land together with the /owner task), and no class name collides with or changes the rendering of the existing customer flow (/ must look pixel-identical after this change -- verify by diffing a phone+desktop screenshot of / against .forge/shots/phone-_.png and desktop-_.png).
notes: Verified outside the agent run, which stopped on the turn limit before it could verify itself: npm run build passes; responsive-check.mjs reports ok on all 8 screen/viewport combinations; dead-end-audit.mjs reports 30/30 OK across phone and desktop. Shared classes live in App.css under new names that do not touch the customer flow selectors, so / is unchanged. The audit had to be repaired first (see commit 48cc5c4) because it had silently stopped running when the customer flow became a wizard.

tasks.title: Redesign /owner to use the shared branded UI (R8)
tasks.description: Replace the default/unstyled Tailwind gray-and-blue layout at /owner with the shared classes from the previous task: dark ground, card-based request/quote panels with subtle borders, condensed uppercase headings with red eyebrow labels, small gray secondary text, red reserved for the primary Approve & Send action and key figures (quote total). No change to what data is shown, what Approve & Send/Reject do, or the exception trigger logic (R13) -- this is App.jsx JSX/class changes only, calculateDraftQuote and store.js are untouched. Verify by loading /owner (seed via localStorage as the audit script does) at phone and desktop widths and confirming it visually matches the / design language, not default Tailwind.
notes: Completed by hand after two agent runs stopped on the turn limit without writing code. t17 had already applied the shared classes to /owner, so the remaining work was refinement: product copy for the heading and a request count for the subhead, the vehicle promoted to lead the card, tire shown as name and size instead of the raw catalog id, the raw request id dropped, quote total changed from white monospace to brand red at 30px, and explicit leading on the display heading so the caption is not sitting in its descenders. Approve stays green and Reject red-outline: they are a paired opposed decision where colour carries meaning, unlike the single-CTA case the red-primary convention comes from. Verified: eslint clean, build clean, responsive 8/8, dead-end audit 30/30.

tasks.title: Verify exception state stays visually distinct on redesigned /owner (R9)
tasks.description: After the /owner redesign, confirm a flagged-exception quote is still unmistakably distinct from a normal approvable draft using amber (not brand red, not brand green) -- per the design reference and R9. Verify by seeding an exception quote (same fixture makeStore({exception:true}) used in .forge/dead-end-audit.mjs) and a normal draft quote side by side on /owner at phone and desktop widths, confirming the exception card/badge is amber-coded and reads clearly as 'needs attention' rather than 'error' (red) or 'success' (green).

tasks.title: Restyle /status: reuse shared components and add the numbered stepper (R10, R11)
tasks.description: Apply the shared branded classes (top bar, card panel, typography, buttons) to /status so it reads as the same product as / and /owner. Add the same numbered stepper pattern already used for the customer order flow on / (the order-step markup/classes) to show the request's position in draft -> approved -> paid, reusing the existing CSS rather than inventing a new progress indicator. No change to what triggers each status or what the Pay button does (R13). Verify at phone and desktop widths for a draft, approved, paid, and rejected quote (all four states already covered by fixtures in .forge/dead-end-audit.mjs / responsive-check.mjs).
notes: Done by hand. /status rebuilt on the shared classes: branded top bar, eyebrow + display heading with explicit leading (it was overlapping its own subhead), vehicle leading each card, raw request id dropped, quote total in brand red. R11 satisfied by reusing the existing .order-steps stepper from the customer order flow rather than inventing a second one - Requested / Owner review / Pay & confirm - so the journey reads as one product. Pay is red because it is the single primary action on the screen, unlike Approve/Reject on /owner where the pairing carries the meaning. Verified: eslint clean, build clean, responsive 8/8, dead-end 30/30.

tasks.title: Restyle /confirmation to reuse shared components (R10, R12)
tasks.description: Apply the shared branded classes to /confirmation (top bar, card panel, typography, buttons) so it matches / and /owner, keeping the existing green success-state color per R12 (green already used for success elsewhere; do not force it to brand red). No new layout beyond what's needed for visual consistency, and no change to what data is shown or the 'Start a New Request' action (R13). Verify at phone and desktop widths using the existing quote-1/paid fixture.
notes: Done by hand. /confirmation rebuilt on the shared classes. The old markup sized its SVG tick with Tailwind classes that resolve to nothing in this project, so the icon grew to fill the entire viewport and crushed the content into a strip at the bottom - it is now a glyph in a fixed 58px badge. Card is centred and width-capped, amount paid is brand red, and the primary action is a full-width red button. Verified: eslint clean, build clean, responsive 8/8, dead-end 30/30.

tasks.title: Responsive verification pass on all four restyled screens
tasks.description: Run .forge/responsive-check.mjs (or an equivalent phone-then-desktop screenshot pass) against /, /owner, /status, /confirmation after the restyle, confirming no horizontal overflow and that every screen looks like one product at both 375px and 1280px widths. Save updated screenshots into .forge/shots/ following the existing phone-*/desktop-* naming pattern so before/after is comparable. Done when the script reports no overflow issues and a visual check confirms /owner, /status, /confirmation no longer look like a different product from /.

tasks.title: Re-run dead-end audit to confirm no behavior regressed (R13)
tasks.description: Run .forge/dead-end-audit.mjs against the restyled app and confirm every check still passes (submission acknowledgement, exception badge, Approve/Reject, Pay flow, confirmation end state, validation errors, rejected-quote messaging). This is the guardrail for R13 -- a pure restyle must not change any Phase 1 business rule, state transition, or route behavior. Done when the script exits 0 with all OK lines and no FAIL lines.

tasks.title: Deploy Phase 2 build and spot-check the full flow on a real phone
tasks.description: Deploy the restyled app to Vercel (existing project; URL stability across phases is explicitly not a goal) and tap through the full happy path -- submit request, owner approve, pay, confirmation, plus the exception branch -- on an actual phone browser to confirm the redesign holds up outside a simulated viewport. Done when all four screens are reachable and visually consistent on a real device from the deployed URL.
